analysis.investment_thesis: Lloyds Engineering is a legitimate fast grower riding India's industrial capex boom — revenue exploded from ₹50Cr to ₹846Cr in 3 years — but at a P/E of 48x with a PEG above 1.5 on any normalized forward growth rate, you're paying full price for a story that still needs to prove it can sustain scale. I'd love this stock 30% cheaper.
key_strengths: Explosive revenue & profit CAGR (~160% over 3 years) across oil & gas, steel, nuclear, and port equipment — multiple end-market tailwinds
Balance sheet discipline: Debt/Equity of just 0.16 despite massive capacity expansion, and FCF finally turned positive at ₹92Cr in FY2025
17% operating margins for a heavy engineering/EPC player are strong, indicating pricing power and project execution quality
key_risks: PEG ratio is stretched: even assuming 30% forward earnings growth, PEG = ~1.6 — well above my comfort zone of <1.0; the market is pricing in perfection
ROCE of only 9.8% is below what a capital-intensive industrial should earn — heavy equity raises (equity jumped ₹777Cr in FY2025 alone) are diluting per-share returns
Growth base effect: ₹50Cr base in 2022 made the CAGR look heroic; sustaining even 25-30% growth from an ₹846Cr revenue base in a lumpy EPC business is genuinely hard
red_flags: Only 1 of last 4 years generated positive operating cash flow — capital-hungry business historically consumed cash before FY2025 turn
Massive equity dilution: total equity nearly tripled in one year (₹411Cr→₹1,188Cr), massively inflating asset base and suppressing per-share metrics
EV/EBITDA of 47.6x for an engineering fabricator is extreme — this is a cyclical business being priced like a technology compounder
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Lloyds Engineering is the kind of company I love to find — a niche industrial equipment maker (marine loading arms, pressure vessels, EPC projects) plugged directly into India's multi-decade infrastructure supercycle. The story is simple, tangible, and visible. Revenue went from ₹50Cr to ₹846Cr in three years; net profit from ₹6Cr to ₹105Cr. Operating margins at 17% are solid for the sector. The company serves oil & gas refineries, port jetties, steel plants, and nuclear facilities — exactly the industries where India is spending massively on domestic manufacturing. Low debt (D/E 0.16) and the first real FCF year (₹92Cr) in FY2025 suggest the business model is beginning to self-fund.

The problem is the price. At P/E 48x on ₹105Cr net profit, the market has already awarded this stock a growth premium that demands flawless execution for years. My PEG calculation — even using an optimistic 30% forward growth assumption — lands at 1.6, which is my hard sell signal. The ROCE at 9.8% tells me the capital deployed so far is earning below what good businesses earn; the massive equity raise (₹777Cr net new equity in FY2025) inflated assets and will weigh on ROE going forward. I'd watch this closely — if growth continues and the stock corrects to a P/E of 30-35x (PEG ~1.0), it becomes a genuine buy. Right now, the story is excellent but the price already tells the story.
